bull_bear.body:
- Second fastest growing company among the top 30 companies in the Indian Pharmaceutical Market by domestic sales between MAT June 2022 and MAT June 2025 (domestic sales CAGR 16.77% vs IPM 9.21%).
- Fastest growing among the top 30 IPM companies by domestic sales between MAT June 2024 and MAT June 2025 (13.58% vs IPM 7.90%).
- Diversified portfolio of 71 brands with 27 'engine' brands contributing 72.34% of domestic sales in MAT June 2025, including market-leading brands Cor, Trazer, Cor9, B-29 and Myoril.
- 'Middle of the pyramid' strategy targeting specialists and super-specialists, who contributed 75.75% of the Company's prescriptions in MAT June 2025 vs 60.96% for the IPM.
- Increasing chronic and sub-chronic mix, rising from 63.82% (MAT June 2022) to 70.10% (MAT June 2025) of domestic sales.
- Pan-India marketing and distribution network with a field force of 2,671 medical representatives across 22 states as of June 30, 2025.
- Market rank improved from 37th (MAT June 2022) to 29th largest pharmaceutical company in India (MAT June 2025).
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Therapeutic-area concentration — Women's healthcare, cardio-diabeto and pain management together contributed 62.40% of FY2025 revenue from operations and 65.14% for the three months ended June 30, 2025; underperformance of these areas would materially affect results.
- Brand concentration — 27 'engine' brands contributed 72.34% of domestic sales in MAT June 2025, so performance is dependent on a limited set of key brands.
- Dependence on specialist prescriptions — Specialists and super-specialists contributed 75.75% of prescriptions in MAT June 2025; changes in prescribing behaviour or access to these doctors could affect sales.
- Pure Offer for Sale — The Company will not receive any proceeds from the Offer; all proceeds go to the Selling Shareholders.
- Reliance on third-party industry data — Industry and market positioning claims rely on the CRISIL Intelligence Report commissioned and paid for by the Company, and reliance on such information is subject to inherent risks.
- Non-GAAP measures — The RHP includes non-Ind AS financial measures that are not standardized and may not be comparable with those presented by other companies.

risks.note: Around 76% of domestic sales come from the 32 Engine Brands, creating dependence on a concentrated set of key brands for revenue.
High dependence on women's healthcare, cardio-diabetes and pain management segments; revenue could be impacted if demand in these therapies slows or competition increases.
West Zone contributes 45.20% of domestic sales, creating regional revenue dependence despite ongoing efforts to expand South and East India coverage.

Dependence on third-party suppliers for APIs and raw materials may cause supply disruptions and cost volatility; partly mitigated via backward integration into hormone APIs through La Chandra Pharmalab.
risks.risk: API and raw material supply risk

risks.note: Pharmaceutical operations are subject to strict regulatory approvals, inspections and price controls across manufacturing facilities.
Price controls under the National List of Essential Medicines can compress product margins; Company states NLEM exposure of 9.76% of sales, which it characterises as lower than the industry average.
Intense competition from both domestic and multinational pharmaceutical companies may affect market share and pricing power.
Imported inputs and overseas business expose the Company to forex fluctuations and supply disruptions, compounded by the ongoing Middle East conflict's effect on shipping routes and freight costs.
